unit.unitOverview: Say what you did yesterday and last week. Use -ed words, and went, had and saw. Ask: Did you go? Answer: Yes, I did. Say the twelve months in order. Read a short story about a lost bag.
unit.learningPath:
The lesson: listen and repeat.
Words: listen, look and say. 28 words.
Patterns: 4 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: a story, the months and a form.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about yesterday. Made-up is OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
Quiz: 12 questions. At the end, My progress.

visual.lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 10.
In this unit, you say what you did.
Today is this day. Yesterday is the day before today.
Listen.
Every day, I walk to the shop.
Yesterday, I walked to the park.
Walk. Walked.
For the past, add -ed to the doing word.
I played. She worked. They visited.
The word is the same for I, you, he, she, we and they.
Listen to the end of these words.
worked, walked, stopped.
played, called, arrived.
Say the end short. Not work-ed. Say: worked.
Now listen: waited, visited.
Here, -ed is one more part. Wait-ed. Vis-it-ed.
Some doing words do not add -ed. They change.
go, went. I went to the city.
have, had. We had tea.
see, saw. She saw a film.
eat, ate. They ate rice.
get, got. He got a new phone.
And five more.
take, took. give, gave. find, found. lose, lost. leave, left.
Say them like this every day: go, went. see, saw.
Now ask about the past. Start with did.
Did you go to the park?
Yes, I did.
No, I didn't.
After did, the word does not change.
Not: Did you went? Say: Did you go?
Say no with didn't.
I didn't go. She didn't see it.
Now, when? Listen to the time words.
now, today, yesterday.
last week, last month, last year.
a week ago, a month ago, a year ago.
Last comes first: last week. No the.
Ago comes at the end: a year ago.
A year has twelve months. Listen and repeat.
January, February, March, April.
May, June, July, August.
September, October, November, December.
Say Feb-ru-ar-y slowly.
Write each month with a capital letter.
Say in with a month: in May, in October.
In Reading, there is a short story.
A woman leaves her bag on a bus. Where is her fish?
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

readings.title: The Green Bag
readings.setting: A shop, a bus and a bus office, on one Friday.
readings.passageScript:
Last Friday, Mia went to the shop.
She got rice, apples and a big fish.
She took the bus with her green bag.
The bus stopped on her street.
At her door, Mia stopped too.
Her bag! She didn't have it.
She left it on the bus!
She called the bus office.
“A green bag? Yes, we have it.”
Mia went to the office and got her bag.
She looked in it. Rice, apples … no fish!
She called the shop.
“Did I leave a fish there?”
“Yes, you did. And your umbrella!”

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 4; Grade 3 Unit 3, Grade 3 Unit 5
grammar.title: -ed for the past: worked, played
grammar.explanation:
Say what you did.
Add -ed to the doing word.
Today I walk. Yesterday I walked.
The same for I, she, we and they.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
work — worked
play — played
help — helped
visit — visited
finish — finished

ends in e: add d
arrive — arrived
close — closed

stop — stopped (two p)

Say the end:
worked, helped, stopped — short
played, called, arrived — short
waited, visited — one more part: wait-ed

The same for all:
I worked. She worked. They worked.
grammar.workedExample:
Yesterday I ___ (walk) to the shop.
1. Yesterday is before today. It is the past.
2. walk: add -ed.
3. walked.
4. Yesterday I walked to the shop.
5. Say it. The end is short: walked.
grammar.commonMistake:
After yesterday, it is easy to write work, not worked.
No: Yesterday I work in the garden.
Yes: Yesterday I worked in the garden.
See a past time word? Look for -ed.
grammar.practice:
Write the past word.
1. Yesterday I ___ (work) in the garden.
2. Last week we ___ (play) football.
3. She ___ (visit) her aunt in May.
4. The bus ___ (stop) near the park.
5. They ___ (arrive) in the evening.
6. I ___ (finish) my book yesterday.
7. He ___ (wait) for the bus.
8. We ___ (call) our grandmother on Sunday.
grammar.answerKey:
1. worked  2. played  3. visited  4. stopped  5. arrived  6. finished  7. waited  8. called
Wrong on 4? stop: stopped. Write two p.
Wrong on 5? arrive ends in e. Add d only: arrived.

grammar.title: Went, had, saw: words that change
grammar.explanation:
Some doing words do not add -ed.
They change.
go: went. eat: ate.
Say them like this: go, went.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
go — went
have — had
see — saw
eat — ate
get — got
take — took
give — gave
find — found
lose — lost
leave — left

I went to the shop.
We had tea.
She saw a film.
They ate rice.
He got a new phone.
I lost my key. I found it!

The same for all:
I went. He went. We went.
grammar.workedExample:
Last week I ___ (see) a film.
1. Last week: a past time.
2. Does see take -ed? No. It is in the list.
3. The list says: see — saw.
4. Last week I saw a film.
5. Check: saw, not seed.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to add -ed to these words.
No: I goed to the shop.
Yes: I went to the shop.
No: We eated rice.
Yes: We ate rice.
grammar.memoryTip: Say them every day: go, went. see, saw.
grammar.practice:
Write the past word.
1. Yesterday I ___ (go) to the city.
2. We ___ (have) tea in the garden.
3. She ___ (see) Omar last week.
4. They ___ (eat) fish and rice.
5. He ___ (get) a new bag.
6. I ___ (lose) my key on Monday.
7. Ben ___ (find) it on the floor.
8. We ___ (leave) the park in the evening.
grammar.answerKey:
1. went  2. had  3. saw  4. ate  5. got  6. lost  7. found  8. left
Wrong on 6 or 7? lose: lost. find: found. They change. No -ed.
Wrong on 8? leave: left. Not leaved.

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 4; Grade 3 Unit 3, Grade 3 Unit 5
grammar.title: Did you go? I didn't go.
grammar.explanation:
Ask about the past with did.
Say no with didn't.
After did and didn't, the doing word does not change.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Did you go to the park?
Yes, I did.
No, I didn't.

Did she see the bus?
Yes, she did.
No, she didn't.

I went. I didn't go.
She saw it. She didn't see it.
We worked. We didn't work.

Where did you go?
What did you eat?

didn't: did not
grammar.workedExample:
Omar went to the office.
Make a question.
1. It is the past. Start with Did.
2. Did Omar …
3. After Did: go, not went.
4. Did Omar go to the office?
5. The answer: Yes, he did.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to keep the past word after did.
No: Did you went to the park?
Yes: Did you go to the park?
No: I didn't saw it.
Yes: I didn't see it.
grammar.memoryTip: Did has the past in it. Go, see and eat do not change.
grammar.practice:
Write the right word.
1. Did you ___ (go / went) to the park?
2. I didn't ___ (see / saw) the bus.
3. ___ (Did / Do) she arrive yesterday?
4. Did they eat fish? No, they ___ (didn't / don't).
5. Did you find your key? Yes, I ___ (did / found).
6. We didn't ___ (took / take) the bus.
7. Where ___ (did / do) you go last week?
grammar.answerKey:
1. go  2. see  3. Did  4. didn't  5. did  6. take  7. did
Wrong on 1, 2 or 6? After did or didn't, the word does not change: go, see, take.
Wrong on 5? A short answer uses did: Yes, I did.
Wrong on 7? Last week is the past, so did.

grammar.title: Yesterday, today, a week ago
grammar.explanation:
Say when with a time word.
Today: this day.
Yesterday: the day before today.
Last week: the week before this one.
A week ago: seven days before now.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
now — I am at the shop now.
today — Today I cooked fish.
yesterday — Yesterday I visited Ana.

last — last Friday, last week, last month, last year
ago — a week ago, two months ago, a year ago

in with a month — in May, in October
on with a day — on Monday

At the start or at the end:
Yesterday I saw Ben.
I saw Ben yesterday.
grammar.workedExample:
Today is Friday.
Mia visited Omar on Thursday.
Say it with a time word.
1. Thursday is the day before Friday.
2. The day before today: yesterday.
3. Mia visited Omar yesterday.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to add the.
No: I saw Ben the last week.
Yes: I saw Ben last week.
It is easy to say ago first.
No: ago a year.
Yes: a year ago.
grammar.memoryTip: Last goes at the start: last week. Ago goes at the end: a week ago.
grammar.practice:
Write yesterday, today, last, ago or in.
1. Today is Friday. Mia arrived on Thursday. She arrived ___.
2. I got my bike a year ___.
3. We visited Hana ___ week.

activities.instructionsAndItems:

1. went  2. visited  3. saw  4. ate  5. walked  6. lost  7. found  8. gave  9. left  10. took

2. We ate fish.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a checklist. The one listening task, Speaking 4, asks the learner to listen before reading. If you are helping, read that talk aloud yourself as a second voice, then let the learner answer before either of you looks at the key.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 4; Grade 3 Unit 3, Grade 3 Unit 5
teacherNotes.noteType: The two errors worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: Dropping -ed after a past time word (Yesterday I work), and keeping the past form after did (Did you went? I didn't saw it). Point at the time word, or at did, rather than giving the answer; the keys explain both. Saying worked with an extra syllable, work-ed, is common and rarely stops the learner being understood. Speaking 1 targets it gently; do not let it crowd out the two above.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 4; Grade 3 Unit 3, Grade 3 Unit 5
teacherNotes.note: Was and were, came, told and felt, last night and two days ago belong to Unit 16, so the texts here avoid them: the story is told with went, got, took and left instead. If a learner asks for I was, it is fine to show it, but nothing here tests it. Clock times with at are Unit 11, which is why times of day appear as in the morning and in the evening.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 4; Grade 3 Unit 3, Grade 3 Unit 5
teacherNotes.note: The months are taught with their order and their number of days, never with weather, seasons or festivals, because those depend on where the learner lives. Keep it that way if you add your own examples.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 4; Grade 3 Unit 3, Grade 3 Unit 5
teacherNotes.note: The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. Tasks say that made-up days, places and things are fine. Never ask a learner when they arrived in a country or where they lived before; the arrive and ago examples in this unit are about bikes, bags and visits for that reason.

1. went  2. visited  3. saw  4. ate  5. walked  6. lost  7. found  8. gave  9. left  10. took
Only numbers 2 and 5 add -ed.
Wrong on 7? find: found. Not finded.
9 or 10 right: good.
8 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance:
1. Did you go to the park?
2. Did she see the bus?
3. Did they eat fish?
4. Where did you go?
5. What did you eat?
6. Did he arrive on Monday?
7. Did you find your key?
Numbers 4 and 5: where or what first, and did second.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance:
1. She didn't see the film.
2. We didn't eat fish.
3. He didn't lose his phone.
4. They didn't arrive on Monday.
5. I didn't finish my book.
6. Mia didn't leave her bag on the bus.
7. We didn't have tea.
Check: after didn't, no -ed and no past word. Not didn't arrived.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance:
1. yesterday  2. ago  3. last  4. today  5. ago  6. in  7. January  8. April  9. August  10. November
Wrong on 2 or 5? Ago comes at the end: a year ago.
Part B: a capital letter on each month.
9 or 10 right: good.
8 or less: read Pattern 4 and Reading 2, and do it again.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance:
1. b  2. c  3. a  4. f  5. e  6. d
Wrong on d? Mia called the shop last, for her fish.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read the story again, line by line.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: worked — Yesterday is the past, so add -ed: worked. Work and works are for every day. Working goes with am, is or are.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: stopped — Stop takes two p before -ed: stopped. Stoped has one p. Stops and stop are not the past.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: visited — Vis-it-ed: the -ed is one more part, like wait-ed. Played, worked and arrived have a short end.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: went — Go changes: go, went. Goed is not a word. Go is not the past. Going goes with am, is or are.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: lost — The key is not in the bag. Lose changes to lost. Found: you have it again. Losed is not a word.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: had — Have changes: have, had. Haved is not a word. Has and have are for every day, not yesterday.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Did — Yesterday is the past, so ask with Did. Do and Does are for every day. Are goes with -ing.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: didn't — No goes with didn't. Did is for Yes. Don't is for every day. Finished says yes, not no.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: I didn't see it. — After didn't, the word does not change: see. Didn't saw has two past words. I not see has no didn't.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: yesterday — Monday is the day before Tuesday, so yesterday. Today is Tuesday. Last year and a week ago are not one day.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: May — January, February, March, April, May: May is fifth. April is fourth. March is third. June is sixth.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: ago — Ago comes at the end: a month ago. Last comes at the start: last month. In goes with a month name. Yesterday is one day.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
